(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum) This appeal is by the claimants
questioning the quantum determined by the Tribunal in MVC.No.62/2016.
The respondent No.2/Insurance company admits its liability.
The appeal is purely on quantum.
2. The appellants who are widow and children of one Abdulsab have filed a claim petition for having lost said Abdulsab in a road traffic accident dated 07.11.2014.

The Tribunal in absence of income proof, notionally assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- without adding future prospects and awarded a sum of Rs.6,24,000/- under the head 'loss of dependency'.

sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2/Insurance company.
4.

Upon a detailed examination of the material on record, this Court is of the considered opinion that the claimant's assertion regarding his employment in the NC: 2024:KHC-K:8541 Agriculture Office at Aurad-B on a contractual basis, with a monthly salary of Rs.9,000/- as reflected in the salary certificate marked as Ex.P-9, remains unsubstantiated.
A key aspect influencing this conclusion is the claimant's failure to produce the author of the said certificate for examination.
In the absence of corroborative evidence or testimony from the issuing authority to authenticate the document, the Tribunal has appropriately declined to assign any evidentiary value to Ex.P-9.
Consequently, the claimant's contention lacks the necessary foundation to be upheld.

5. In absence of income proof, having regard to the fact that accident is of the year 2014, this Court is inclined to rely on the income chart prepared by the Legal Services Authority and the income is notionally assessed at Rs.7,500/-.
Deceased was aged 50 years and therefore, 10% needs to be added towards future prospects and the income is taken at Rs.8,250/-.
After deducting 1/4th and by applying multiplier of 13, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:8541 compensation re-determined under the head 'loss of dependency' works out to Rs.9,65,250/- (8,250x12x13x1/4).
6. Since there are four dependents, a sum of Rs.1,90,000/- is awarded under conventional heads which includes loss of estate and funeral expenses.

In terms of dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.1, 10% escalation for every three years which works out to Rs.38,000/- is added.
